title: Follow-Through, Recovery & Professional Responsibility
summary: Bring the unit together by learning how to recover from missed commitments, restore trust through follow-through, and improve future reliability.
objectives: Identify responsible actions after a missed or delayed commitment.
Distinguish accountability from excuses or unnecessary self-blame.
Create a practical recovery and prevention plan.

vocab.def: Completing an agreed responsibility or carrying out the next action you committed to take.
Taking responsibility for actions, commitments, impacts, and appropriate next steps.
Actions taken to address the impact of a problem and restore progress.
A change intended to reduce the likelihood of the same problem happening again.

sections.heading: A missed commitment is not the end of responsibility
sections.body: When something is missed or delayed, responsibility includes addressing the impact rather than simply explaining what happened.

sections.heading: Accountability focuses on what happens next
sections.body: A professional response identifies the commitment, acknowledges the impact when appropriate, communicates the current status, and takes the next agreed action.

sections.heading: Recovery should be realistic
sections.body: Do not promise an impossible deadline just to make a situation sound better. A recovery plan should reflect actual capacity, dependencies, approvals, and available resources.

sections.heading: Use patterns to improve reliability
sections.body: Repeated lateness, missed deadlines, overloaded schedules, or forgotten tasks may indicate a planning problem. Improvement can include earlier preparation, better reminders, clearer priorities, more realistic estimates, or earlier communication.

practice.prompt: You miss a deadline. Is saying 'I was busy' enough to demonstrate professional accountability?
practice.answer: No. Accountability also includes communicating status, addressing the impact, and agreeing on a realistic next step.

practice.prompt: You notice that you repeatedly underestimate how long assignments take. What improvement could help?
practice.answer: Use more realistic estimates, checkpoints, and buffers based on what previous work actually required.

quiz.question: What best demonstrates follow-through after a missed commitment?
options: Acknowledge the impact, communicate a realistic recovery plan, and complete the agreed next steps
Explain why someone else should have prevented the problem
quiz.answer: Acknowledge the impact, communicate a realistic recovery plan, and complete the agreed next steps

lab.objective: Review a simulated missed commitment and create a recovery plan containing status, impact, next actions, timing, communication, and one prevention improvement.

reflectionPrompt: How can the way you respond after a mistake or delay affect whether other people continue to trust you?
